role: Global GSI Lead, Healthcare and Life Sciences Ecosystem
jobDescription:
NVIDIA is hiring a Global GSI Lead, Healthcare and Life Sciences Ecosystem (Developer Relations Manager, GSI Partnerships). This leadership position focuses on incubating business within the Healthcare and Life Sciences ecosystem globally, with the goal of accelerating the adoption and proliferation of AI across the HCLS sector. The role reports into Kimberly Powell's Healthcare and Life Sciences organization and is responsible for scaling NVIDIA's HCLS business through strategic Global System Integrator (GSI) partners — Accenture, Deloitte, Wipro, Capgemini, Infosys, TCS, HCL, IBM Consulting, Cognizant, and similar firms.

What you'll be doing:
- Lead joint solution development with major GSI partners, integrating NVIDIA AI technology (Clara, BioNeMo, Parabricks, MONAI, Holoscan, NIM microservices, NeMo, DGX, Blackwell) into their offerings and enabling new AI services.
- Develop and complete strategic go-to-market plans with GSIs to accelerate AI adoption and drive growth in the Healthcare and Life Sciences sector.
- Drive revenue and pipeline growth by championing NVIDIA's hardware, software, and partner ecosystem in HCLS-specific solutions.
- Collaborate cross-functionally across NVIDIA and with partners to hit targets, enable GSI teams, and advance mutual thought leadership.

What they need to see:
- Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
- 12+ years in complex sales or partner business management, with 10+ years managing large GSIs globally.
- Proven ability to build and implement complex go-to-market strategies across matrixed organizations.
- Deep domain & product expertise, including developing and launching Healthcare and Life Sciences-specific joint solutions.
- Extensive knowledge of GSI operations, enterprise computing software/services, and a track record of successful joint solutioning and GTM with partners.
- Outstanding partner and customer relationship skills; ability to influence without direct authority.
- High energy, proactive, and adaptable; strong communication skills for technical and executive audiences.
- Familiarity with modern computing techniques, AI markets within HCLS, and NVIDIA products/services.

Stand out criteria:
- Expertise in Healthcare and Life Sciences AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning applications.
- Experience in joint solutioning (product management background is a plus).
- Track record of driving strategic growth through partnerships.
- Experience with cloud, Generative AI, and Agentic AI.
- Proficiency in leading complex global programs and diverse customer engagements.

Compensation: $224K–$356.5K base + equity + benefits. Applications accepted through April 12, 2026.
emphasisAreas: Healthcare and Life Sciences AI domain expertise — Arine (payor/health-plan systems, 30M+ members, 45+ plans), Booz Allen (FDA/CDRH AI governance policy in response to Executive Order 14110, population/predictive medicine, FedRAMP/HIPAA), TReNDS Center (GPU deep-learning infrastructure for neuroimaging and genomics on COINSTAC with differential privacy), NeuroLex Labs (voice computing for neurodegenerative disease), Hyperbloom (healthcare, life science, and financial services consulting with clinical-trial clients like Florence Healthcare)

GPU and accelerated computing depth — built and operated GPU compute infrastructure for deep learning at TReNDS Center for COINSTAC; runs NVIDIA RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 workstations locally for daily LLM experimentation (Ollama, LM Studio, Open WebUI); benchmarked and ran inference workloads on both AWS and Azure GPU fleets; understands the TCO, networking, and orchestration tradeoffs NVIDIA GSI partners face when sizing DGX, HGX, and Blackwell deployments for customers

Global System Integrator partner experience — at Microsoft (Fortune 100 customers + global delivery teams, including Deloitte, HP, Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, AmerisourceBergen, BlueCross BlueShield), at Slalom Consulting (acted AS a GSI partnering with Microsoft Azure as the tech vendor; delivered joint solutions to healthcare and public sector clients), at AWS (partnered with Deloitte and Accenture as co-sell GSIs serving enterprise accounts; grew AWS AI/ML adoption through consulting partner motion), at Booz Allen (partnered with AWS as the cloud GSI for federal healthcare workloads), at Hyperbloom (partnered with AWS, boutique consulting firms, and research organizations like TReNDS Center)

Joint solutioning and co-innovation with partners — shipped joint Microsoft + Azure Bot Service vs. Amazon Lex assessments for Fortune 100 insurance clients, published AWS reference architectures, wrote SBIR research grants, and commercialized open-source research into industry partnerships at TReNDS; this is the exact muscle NVIDIA needs for GSI co-innovation labs (Lilly/NVIDIA LLM co-innovation lab pattern)

Executive relationship building and influence without authority — built deep C-suite relationships at AWS across Cox Enterprises, Cox Automotive, Equifax, NCR, Jostens, and D3; engaged nationally as an AI/ML subject matter expert across private and public events; Fortune 100 escalation contact at Microsoft during critical deployments; trusted advisor role at Booz Allen to federal health leadership

Healthcare regulatory and compliance depth — HIPAA (8+ years), FDA/CDRH AI governance policy drafting work at Booz Allen in response to President Biden's Executive Order 14110, FedRAMP environments, differential privacy for PHI protection on COINSTAC, public health data integration at Booz Allen for FDA and CDRH clients including vaccine supply chain analytics, clinical trials work via Florence Healthcare, DBHDD behavioral health systems at Slalom, and HL7/CDISC/SDTM/ADaM interoperability standards

Agentic AI and Generative AI production experience — designs and operates multi-agent LLM systems daily; at Arine, designed the AI DataOps Toolkit and built the observability pipeline for Arine's autonomous pharmacist AI agent; at Modular Earth, architected a 6-stage multi-agent workflow with role-based permissions and structured handoffs; at paulprae.com, ships a live AI career assistant using Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Vercel AI SDK; runs local LLMs on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and 5090 hardware; expert in Claude, OpenAI, and Anthropic APIs as well as open models via Ollama and LM Studio

Complex, global, matrixed program leadership — 13+ years leading cross-functional teams of engineers, data scientists, account managers, and solutions architects across AWS, Slalom, Booz Allen, Hyperbloom, Decooda, NeuroLex, and Microsoft; Microsoft MACH graduate; nominated for Global Business Support's Entrepreneur of the Year (2013); delivered projects across more than 10 healthcare, life sciences, financial services, and public sector clients

Proven revenue and pipeline impact — $1.4M ARR built from $40K investment at Hyperbloom; $2M+ consulting revenue from a single Slalom engagement; managed an AWS portfolio of 10+ enterprise accounts; shipped production systems at Red Ventures partnering on marketing technology that drove customer acquisition for 16+ Fortune 500 brands including DirecTV, AT&T, Verizon, Liberty Mutual, and Progressive

Thought leadership, evangelism, and content — national speaker on AI, NLP, and ML at AWS, Slalom, and Microsoft events; author of technical whitepapers, reference architectures, and presentations published via SlideShare and Frontiers in Neuroinformatics; co-author of peer-reviewed publication on federated neuroimaging analysis using differential privacy (2023); published GitHub open-source work under the Modular Earth organization

Go-to-market strategy development for healthcare and life sciences — at Hyperbloom (hyperbloom.ai), built the entire GTM motion for an AI consulting business delivering cloud-based AI and data solutions to healthcare, life science, and financial services customers; defined ideal customer profiles, messaging, pricing, packaging, partner co-sell motion, SOW templates, and the full sales cycle; led sales coordinators, account managers, and solutions architects through lead-to-close; partnered with AWS, boutique consulting firms, and research organizations like TReNDS Center to source and close deals; grew to $1.4M ARR from a $40K investment. This is the exact GTM muscle NVIDIA needs from its GSI Lead — the ability to work backwards from a partner's P&L and build joint GTM plans that move both companies' numbers.

Solutions architect as a career-long identity — 13 years spent architecting production systems across every layer of the stack: enterprise AI/ML architecture at AWS (Bedrock, SageMaker, ECS/EKS); cloud data platforms at Arine (Snowflake + AWS, petabyte scale); GPU compute and federated research infrastructure at TReNDS Center for COINSTAC; AI consulting delivery architecture at Booz Allen, Hyperbloom, Slalom, and Decooda; enterprise Microsoft ecosystem architecture at Slalom and Microsoft; full-stack marketing-technology architecture at Red Ventures. Titles held: Principal AI Architect, Chief AI Architect, Senior AI Solutions Architect, Enterprise AI and ML Solutions Architect, Neuroinformatics Data Platform Architect. Solution architecture is the through-line across every single role since 2014. This is the identity to lead with — NVIDIA's GSI partners expect their NVIDIA counterpart to speak architecture fluently from the very first meeting.
targetAudience:
Primary hiring panel: the NVIDIA Healthcare and Life Sciences leadership team under Kimberly Powell (VP, Healthcare at NVIDIA). This team owns Clara, BioNeMo, Parabricks, MONAI, Holoscan, the Lilly $1B co-innovation lab (LillyPod AI factory with 1,016 Blackwell Ultra GPUs), the Illumina genomics partnership, the Mayo Clinic DGX B200 pathology collaboration, the Roche 3,500+ Blackwell GPU deployment, the IQVIA.ai pharma analytics partnership, and the 5,000+ member Inception healthcare startup program. They are optimizing for a leader who can scale these wins through Accenture, Deloitte, Wipro, Capgemini, Infosys, TCS, HCL, IBM Consulting, and Cognizant — the big GSIs whose consultants actually put NVIDIA technology into hospitals, payors, pharmas, and clinical research organizations.

Secondary audience: NVIDIA Worldwide Field Operations (WWFO) and the NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) leaders responsible for GSI co-sell motion, joint GTM plans, and partner enablement. They care about pipeline hygiene, joint-solution velocity, revenue attribution across a highly matrixed org, and the ability to navigate conflict between NVIDIA's direct sales team and partner-led deals.

All audiences will scan for: (1) deep personal credibility in HCLS AI — not just sales talk, but having actually built and shipped HCLS AI systems; (2) real GSI operator experience — having sat on both sides of the table, both AS a GSI (Slalom, Booz Allen, Hyperbloom) and WITH GSIs (AWS, Microsoft); (3) GPU and accelerated-computing fluency — so joint solution conversations with GSI architects don't need translation; (4) track record of influencing without authority across matrixed, global organizations; (5) executive presence to represent NVIDIA in C-suite conversations with pharma, payor, provider, and medtech leadership.
additionalContext:
NVIDIA's HCLS strategy in 2026 centers on an agentic AI inflection point. At GTC 2026, NVIDIA announced the open-source Agent Toolkit, the Rheo hospital digital twin blueprint, Hippocratic AI's agentic patient monitoring, and a flood of partner deployments. Kimberly Powell publicly frames the moment as 'the transformer moment for biology and drug discovery' and notes healthcare is deploying AI at more than 2x the rate of the broader economy. The $4.9T HCLS sector is the single largest industry NVIDIA is verticalizing.

Paul's unique wedge for this role: he is one of very few candidates who can credibly speak to (1) healthcare AI engineering depth at scale — Arine touches 30M+ members, 45+ health plans; Booz Allen work spanned FDA CDRH, CDC, and FedRAMP healthcare environments; clinical-trial infrastructure via Florence Healthcare and Veeva-adjacent work at Hyperbloom; financial/privacy algorithms via Equifax engagements at AWS and COINSTAC differential-privacy research at TReNDS — AND (2) GSI go-to-market operating experience on BOTH sides — as a Slalom consultant selling Microsoft Azure into healthcare, as an AWS Enterprise SA driving revenue through Deloitte and Accenture co-sell, as a Booz Allen Chief AI Architect partnering with AWS to deliver federal healthcare workloads, and as the founder of Hyperbloom partnering with AWS and research institutions — AND (3) deep GPU and accelerated-computing fluency — he runs NVIDIA RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 workstations for daily LLM development (Ollama, LM Studio, Open WebUI), architected GPU compute infrastructure at TReNDS for COINSTAC deep-learning workloads, and holds AWS ML Specialty, AWS ML Engineer, and AWS AI Practitioner certifications.

Critical positioning priorities:
1. Lead with the healthcare + GSI fusion. Open the summary with something like 'AI leader combining 10+ years of healthcare and life sciences AI delivery with partner and GSI go-to-market experience across AWS, Microsoft, Booz Allen, Slalom, and Hyperbloom.'
2. Reframe the AWS role as a PARTNER + GSI role, not just a solutions-architecture role. At AWS, Paul co-sold with Deloitte and Accenture and grew AWS revenue through the consulting partner motion. Call that out explicitly — this is NVIDIA's exact playbook.
3. Reframe Slalom, Hyperbloom, and Booz Allen as GSI-side experience. Paul has operated AS a GSI consultant partnering with hyperscaler and tech vendors. He knows how Accenture, Deloitte, Wipro, and Capgemini run internally because he has lived that model.
4. Call out NVIDIA-adjacent technical depth: GPU infrastructure at TReNDS for COINSTAC deep learning; RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 local AI servers running Ollama, LM Studio, and Open WebUI daily; benchmarking and production experience with accelerated workloads on both AWS and Azure GPU families.
5. Call out healthcare regulatory depth that NVIDIA needs from its GSI lead: HIPAA, FDA CDRH AI governance policy drafting at Booz Allen in response to Biden's Executive Order 14110, FedRAMP, differential privacy for PHI, HL7/CDISC/SDTM/ADaM interoperability, and clinical-trial disaster-recovery architecture (Florence Healthcare via Hyperbloom).
6. Ensure the Arine bullet highlights its payor-scale impact — 30M+ members across 45+ plans on Snowflake and AWS — because NVIDIA's GSI partners are selling into exactly these kinds of payor and health-plan environments.
7. Keep the resume to approximately 2 pages when rendered. Lead each role with a partner/GSI or healthcare-AI frame where possible.
8. Lead the professional summary with SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT identity and the healthcare + GSI fusion. Paul has held architect titles continuously since 2014 (Principal AI Architect, Chief AI Architect, Senior AI Solutions Architect, Enterprise AI and ML Solutions Architect, Neuroinformatics Data Platform Architect). This is the identity NVIDIA GSI partners will expect.
9. Weave Hyperbloom GTM work through the Chief AI Officer bullets. Emphasize that Paul built the full GTM motion for a healthcare/life-science AI consulting business (see hyperbloom.ai) — ICP definition, messaging, pricing, partner co-sell, SOW templates, lead-to-close sales cycle — and grew the business to $1.4M ARR from $40K. This directly maps to the joint GTM work NVIDIA expects from its GSI Lead.
10. NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) and Inception program are the two programs Paul's hire would most directly work with, alongside the Healthcare Alliance. The Healthcare Inception cohort alone has 5,000+ member startups and 2,000+ digital-health members. Mentioning relevant ecosystem programs (NPN, Inception, Alliance for Healthcare) in the summary or objective is a signal of ecosystem literacy.
11. Do NOT fabricate numbers, titles, specific client names, or partnership details beyond what is already in the career data. When in doubt, use generic 'Fortune 500 pharma,' 'federal health agency,' or 'payor organization' phrasing. Facts Paul explicitly confirmed to rely on: (a) FDA CDRH AI governance policy drafting at Booz Allen in response to Biden EO 14110; (b) FDA and CDRH as Booz Allen clients including vaccine supply chain analytics work; (c) Florence Healthcare as a clinical trial client of Hyperbloom; (d) DBHDD as a Slalom healthcare client; (e) Equifax as an AWS client; (f) Microsoft MACH graduate; (g) TReNDS Center commercialization via SBIR grants; (h) Accenture and Deloitte as AWS co-sell partners. Everything else should come from the committed career-data.json.
